literal: Those who reprove who does not have, the unsecure king, destroyers even if he is without, will perish.
translation: A king who lacks the security of counselors who boldly reprove him will perish, even if he has no enemies to destroy him.
modern: தன் தவறுகளைக் கண்டித்துத் திருத்தும் பெரியோர்களைத் துணையாகக் கொள்ளாத பாதுகாப்பற்ற மன்னன், தன்னை அழிக்க நினைக்கும் பகைவர்கள் இல்லாவிட்டாலும் தானாகவே அழிந்து போவான்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of having wise counselors who are not afraid to criticize the ruler. The word 'இடிப்பார்' (those who strike or reprove) vividly describes advisors who forcefully point out faults to keep the leader on the right path. The term 'ஏமரா' (unprotected or unsecure) shows that true security for a leader comes from these critical voices, not just from armies or fortresses. Without such guidance, a ruler will inevitably make fatal mistakes and ruin himself, even if there are no external enemies actively trying to bring him down.
